question: A stakeholder has submitted the requirement "make monthly reporting easier." An analyst wants Claude to help prepare for the next stakeholder meeting. Which use of Claude is most appropriate here?
options: A) Ask Claude to rewrite the requirement in formal language so it can be entered into the requirements log.
B) Ask Claude to describe how comparable organisations define easier reporting and adopt that wording.
C) Ask Claude to decide which reading the stakeholder most likely meant, and then build the entire delivery plan on it.
D) Ask Claude to produce several plausible readings of the requirement plus questions to put to the stakeholder.
correct_answers: D) Ask Claude to produce several plausible readings of the requirement plus questions to put to the stakeholder.
explanations: Formalising the language makes a vague requirement look rigorous without adding any information. The log then contains a polished statement that still cannot be built or tested, and the ambiguity survives into design.

Adopting an external definition replaces this stakeholder's need with a generic one. It also produces confident-sounding wording that nobody in the organisation has agreed to, which makes the ambiguity harder to spot later, not easier.

Letting Claude pick the most likely reading converts an open question into a hidden assumption. The stakeholder is available to answer, so guessing on their behalf trades a cheap clarification for an expensive misunderstanding.

Correct. Ambiguity is resolved by the stakeholder, not by the tool. Claude is best used here to widen the analyst's view of what the phrase could mean and to generate the specific questions that will close it, so the meeting produces a decision rather than another vague line.
